$comment: Build profiles for EAS. Two things this file deliberately does NOT declare,
because declaring them would describe a capability that does not exist:
1. No `channel` on preview or production. A channel routes an over-the-air
update to a build, and this app has no update mechanism: `expo-updates`
is not a dependency and app.json carries no `updates` or `runtimeVersion`.
The two channel keys that used to be here resolved to nothing. Adding OTA
updates is Round 7 infrastructure work; when it lands, the channels come
back alongside the runtime that reads them.
2. No `submit.production` block. Store submission needs an Apple team and
ASC key, and a Google service account — credentials Round 7 provisions.
An empty object read as configured-and-ready; its absence reads as what
is true.
`appVersionSource: remote` requires a linked EAS project, and none is linked
(there is no `extra.eas.projectId` in app.json or app.config.js). Until
`eas init` runs against a real account, no profile here can build
non-interactively. That is recorded in DESIGN-GAPS.md rather than hidden by
a placeholder id.
Preview and production supply EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_API_ORIGIN and
EXPO_PUBLIC_NATIVE_REDIRECT_URI from the build environment, not from this
file: the redirect URI must string-match the Edge's NATIVE_APP_REDIRECT_URIS
for the deployment being built, and the origin is a real HTTPS Edge.
app.config.js throws when either is missing on a release profile, so a
misconfigured cloud build fails at config time rather than shipping a client
pointed at nothing.
